tadasana-mountain-pose.name: Tadasana (Mountain Pose)
tadasana-mountain-pose.summary: Mountain Pose is a foundational standing posture that aligns the body and improves balance. It is used to develop awareness of alignment and prepare for more complex poses.
benefits: Calms the mind and reduces stress

steps.text: Stand with feet hip‑width apart, big toes touching, weight evenly distributed
Ground through all four corners of each foot—heel, ball, big toe, little toe
Engage the thigh muscles, lift the kneecaps, and gently tuck the tailbone
Lengthen the spine, lift the crown of the head, and relax shoulders away from ears
Breathe deeply, maintaining the alignment, and hold for the desired time

tadasana-mountain-pose.breathing: Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to deepen the grounding, maintaining smooth, even breaths throughout.

common_mistakes.fix: Keep a micro‑bend in the knees to maintain joint safety
Roll shoulders back and down, opening the chest
Keep the heels firmly planted on the floor

easier: Place a block between the thighs to cue engagement
Stand with back against a wall for extra support
harder: Raise arms overhead, palms together, maintaining alignment
Close eyes to challenge balance
props: Yoga block between thighs – helps engage leg muscles
Wall behind – provides tactile feedback for grounding
avoid_if: Severe low blood pressure or dizziness

surya-namaskara-sun-salutation.name: Surya Namaskara (Sun Salutation)
surya-namaskara-sun-salutation.summary: A flowing sequence of twelve linked poses that warms the body and raises heart rate. It is used to improve overall mobility and support calorie expenditure.

steps.text: Begin in Pranamasana, feet together, hands at heart center
Sweep arms up, arch back slightly into Hastauttanasana
Fold forward, placing hands on the floor in Uttanasana
Step right foot back, lower knee, lift chest into Ashwa Sanchalanasana
Slide left foot back, straighten legs into Dandasana (Plank)
Lower hips, chest and chin to the floor, then inhale into Bhujangasana
Press hips up and back, forming Adho Mukha Svanasana
Step right foot forward into Ashwa Sanchalanasana, left foot follows to Uttanasana
Sweep arms up, return to Hastauttanasana
Finish standing tall in Tadasana, palms together

surya-namaskara-sun-salutation.breathing: Coordinate each movement with a smooth inhale or exhale, maintaining steady diaphragmatic breathing throughout.

common_mistakes.mistake: Collapsing the lower back in Bhujangasana
common_mistakes.fix: Lift chest using back muscles, keep pelvis grounded
Slightly bend knees to protect the joint

easier: Place hands on blocks in Uttanasana
Modify Ashwa Sanchalanasana with a shorter step back
harder: Add a deeper backbend in Bhujangasana
Transition to Chaturanga Dandasana before Upward Dog
props: Yoga block under hands in forward folds for extra support

padmasana-lotus-pose.name: Padmasana (Lotus Pose)
padmasana-lotus-pose.summary: Lotus Pose is a seated meditation posture with each foot placed on the opposite thigh. It is used to create a stable, upright seat for focused breathing and calm awareness.

steps.text: Sit on a folded blanket with legs extended in front of you
Bend the right knee and place the right foot on the left thigh, sole up
Bend the left knee and place the left foot on the right thigh, sole up
Lengthen the spine, roll the shoulders back, and relax the jaw
Rest hands on the knees in a comfortable mudra or simply palms down
Close the eyes, soften the gaze, and maintain steady, natural breathing
Hold the pose for the desired duration, maintaining even breath

padmasana-lotus-pose.breathing: Keep the breath smooth and even, inhaling and exhaling through the nose throughout the hold.

common_mistakes.fix: Engage the inner thigh muscles to keep knees aligned with hips
Lengthen the crown of the head toward the floor to maintain a neutral spine

easier: Sit on a folded blanket or block to elevate hips
Use half‑lotus (one foot on opposite thigh)
Sit in a simple cross‑legged position (Sukhasana)
harder: Bind the hands behind the back in a reverse prayer
Extend arms overhead with palms facing each other
Increase hold time beyond 20 minutes
props: Blanket under sit bones for hip support
Yoga block under knees to reduce strain

balasana-child-s-pose.name: Balasana (Child's Pose)
balasana-child-s-pose.summary: Balasana is a resting pose performed on the knees that gently stretches the hips, thighs, and lower back. It is used to calm the nervous system and reduce stress.

steps.text: Kneel on the mat with big toes touching and knees hip‑width apart
Sit back onto your heels, allowing the buttocks to rest on the heels
Fold forward, extending your arms forward or alongside the body
Rest your forehead on the mat, relaxing the neck
Lengthen the spine and breathe deeply, staying for the desired time

balasana-child-s-pose.breathing: Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to deepen the stretch, maintaining smooth, diaphragmatic breathing throughout.

common_mistakes.mistake: Knees too wide, causing strain on the hips
common_mistakes.fix: Keep knees hip‑width or slightly wider for comfort

common_mistakes.mistake: Head not resting, causing neck tension
common_mistakes.fix: Allow the forehead to gently touch the mat

easier: Place a folded blanket under the chest for extra support
Widen the knees more for a larger opening
harder: Extend arms overhead, creating a deeper stretch in the shoulders
Thread one arm under the other for a shoulder stretch
props: Blanket under chest to support the torso
Bolster under the torso for a restorative variation
avoid_if: Pregnant women in the third trimester

vrikshasana-tree-pose.name: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose)
vrikshasana-tree-pose.summary: Tree Pose is a standing balance that strengthens the legs and core while sharpening concentration. Practitioners use it to develop steadiness and confidence in everyday movement.

steps.text: Begin in Tadasana with feet hip‑width apart and arms at your sides
Shift weight onto your left foot, grounding the whole foot into the mat
Bend the right knee and place the right foot on the inner left thigh or calf, avoiding the knee joint
Press the foot into the leg and the leg into the foot, drawing the thigh upward
Bring palms together at the heart center or raise arms overhead, lengthening the spine
Gaze softly at a fixed point (drishti) in front of you to maintain balance
Hold the pose, breathing evenly, then gently release and repeat on the opposite side

vrikshasana-tree-pose.breathing: Maintain slow, steady breaths, inhaling to lengthen and exhaling to stay grounded.

common_mistakes.mistake: Foot placed too high on the knee
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the foot below the knee on the thigh or calf
Engage the standing leg and draw the hips toward the center
Enter the pose slowly and maintain steady breathing throughout

easier: Place the sole of the lifted foot against the ankle or shin instead of the thigh
Use a wall for light support
Keep hands on hips instead of overhead
harder: Close the eyes to challenge proprioception
Extend arms overhead with palms facing each other
Transition from Tree Pose into a standing forward fold
props: Yoga block against the wall for light support
Chair to rest the lifted foot on if balance is limited

bhujangasana-cobra-pose.name: Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose)
bhujangasana-cobra-pose.summary: Cobra Pose is a gentle backbend performed while lying prone, lifting the chest off the floor. It strengthens the spinal extensors, opens the chest, and can ease lower‑back tension.

steps.text: Lie face down with your forehead resting on the mat and legs extended, tops of feet pressing into the floor
Place your hands on the mat directly under your shoulders, elbows close to your body
Press your pubic bone into the floor and engage your core
As you inhale, gently lift your chest using the muscles of your back, keeping elbows slightly bent
Draw your shoulder blades down and away from your ears, gaze forward or slightly upward
Hold the lift for the prescribed time, breathing evenly
To release, exhale and slowly lower your chest back to the mat

bhujangasana-cobra-pose.breathing: Maintain smooth, even breaths, inhaling to lift and exhaling to lower.

common_mistakes.mistake: Overallizing the lift with the arms
common_mistakes.fix: Lead the rise with the back muscles, keep elbows soft
Depress shoulder blades and keep neck long

common_mistakes.mistake: Overall arching causing lower back strain
common_mistakes.fix: Limit lift to a comfortable height, keep pelvis grounded

easier: Place a folded blanket under the hips for extra support
Keep elbows bent more and lift only a few inches
harder: Press firmly through the hands to straighten the arms more fully
Lift deeper by engaging the glutes and lengthening the tailbone
props: Yoga block under the chest to reduce the lift height
Strap around the forearms to maintain even pressure

adho-mukha-svanasana-downward-dog.name: Adho Mukha Svanasana (Downward Dog)
adho-mukha-svanasana-downward-dog.summary: Downward Dog is a full‑body inversion that builds strength in the arms, legs, and core while lengthening the spine. Practitioners use it to improve posture, increase flexibility, and reset the nervous system.

steps.text: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips
Tuck your toes under and press the heels toward the floor
Lift your hips up and back, creating an inverted V shape
Straighten the legs as much as comfortable, keeping a slight bend in the knees if needed
Press firmly through the palms, spreading the fingers wide
Draw the shoulder blades down the back and engage the core
Hold the pose, breathing evenly, then gently release back to tabletop

adho-mukha-svanasana-downward-dog.breathing: Maintain steady, diaphragmatic breaths, inhaling as you lift and exhaling as you settle deeper into the stretch.

common_mistakes.fix: Press the crown toward the thighs to lengthen the spine
Keep a micro‑bend in the knees to allow hamstring release

common_mistakes.mistake: Hands too far forward, shoulders hunched
common_mistakes.fix: Shift weight forward slightly and draw shoulders away from ears

easier: Bend the knees slightly to reduce hamstring tension
Place a block under the hands for extra wrist support
harder: Lift one leg toward the ceiling for a three‑leg variation
Walk the hands farther forward to deepen the stretch
props: Yoga block under each hand to reduce wrist strain
Strap around the forearms for added stability
avoid_if: Wrist pain or carpal tunnel syndrome

virabhadrasana-i-warrior-i.name: Virabhadrasana I (Warrior I)
virabhadrasana-i-warrior-i.summary: Warrior I is a standing strength pose that builds leg power and opens the hips. Practitioners use it to improve balance, posture, and a sense of grounded confidence.

steps.text: Step your right foot forward about 3‑4 feet and turn your left foot out 45 degrees
Bend the right knee so the thigh is parallel to the floor, aligning the knee over the ankle
Square your hips and shoulders toward the front of the mat
Reach both arms overhead, palms facing each other, and lengthen through the spine
Gaze forward or slightly upward, engage the core, and hold the position

virabhadrasana-i-warrior-i.breathing: Maintain steady, diaphragmatic breathing, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the bend.

common_mistakes.fix: Press the knee outward toward the second toe

common_mistakes.mistake: Hips rotate toward the back leg
common_mistakes.fix: Keep hips facing forward, using a wall for cueing

easier: Place hands on hips for balance
Shorten the stance distance
Use a block under the back heel
harder: Lift the back heel off the ground
Add a gentle backbend by opening the chest
Transition into Warrior I to Warrior II flow
props: Yoga block under back heel for stability
Strap around the front thigh to cue alignment

ustrasana-camel-pose.name: Ustrasana (Camel Pose)
ustrasana-camel-pose.summary: Camel Pose is a kneeling backbend that opens the chest and stretches the front body. It builds spinal flexibility and strengthens the back, hips, and core.
benefits: Stretches the front of the body

steps.text: Kneel on the mat with knees hip‑width apart and shins parallel
Place your hands on the lower back with fingers pointing down
Engage the core, lift the chest, and lengthen the tailbone toward the floor
Slowly reach back, grasping the heels (or use a strap) while keeping shoulders relaxed
Press the hips forward, keep the thighs engaged, and allow the head to drop back gently
Hold the pose, breathing evenly
To exit, release the heels, bring the hands to the hips, and slowly rise to a kneeling position

ustrasana-camel-pose.breathing: Maintain smooth, diaphragmatic breathing, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the backbend.

common_mistakes.fix: Engage the core and keep the tailbone tucked slightly
Keep the neck relaxed; look gently upward or keep the chin tucked

easier: Place a block between the heels and hands
Keep hands on the sacrum instead of reaching for heels
harder: Straighten the arms and grasp the heels directly
Add a gentle backbend lift by pressing the hips forward more
props: Yoga block: hold in hands to reduce reach distance
Strap: loop around heels for those with limited flexibility

halasana-plow-pose.name: Halasana (Plow Pose)
halasana-plow-pose.summary: Halasana is an inversion where the legs are lowered over the head, stretching the spine and shoulders. Practitioners use it to calm the nervous system and aid digestion.

steps.text: Lie on your back with arms resting alongside the body, palms facing down
Press into your hands and lift both legs to a 90‑degree angle
Place your hands on your lower back for support as you begin to lower the legs
Slowly guide the legs over your head, keeping them straight and together, until toes touch the floor behind you
If needed, adjust the hands to support the sacrum or keep them on the floor for balance
Hold the pose, breathing evenly, then roll down vertebra by vertebra to release

halasana-plow-pose.breathing: Maintain slow, steady breaths, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the stretch.

common_mistakes.fix: Keep the neck relaxed, use a folded blanket under the shoulders for support
Engage the thighs to keep legs straight and together

easier: Place a folded blanket under the shoulders
Bend the knees and keep shins on the floor
Use a wall to support the legs
harder: Straighten legs fully and press toes into the floor
Interlace fingers behind the back for a deeper shoulder stretch
props: Blanket under shoulders – cushions the neck and supports the
Bolster against the lower back – provides extra support for
Wall – allows legs to rest against for stability
avoid_if: Neck injury or cervical spine issues

cat-cow-stretch.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
cat-cow-stretch.summary: Cat-Cow is a gentle, synchronized movement of the spine performed on hands and knees. It warms the back, releases tension in the neck and improves spinal flexibility.
benefits: Reduces neck and upper back tension
Improves coordination of breath and movement

steps.text: Start on hands and knees in a neutral tabletop position, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale, drop your belly, lift your chest and tailbone, and look up toward the ceiling (Cow).
Exhale, round your spine, draw your belly toward your spine, and tuck your chin toward your chest (Cat).
Continue to flow, moving with each breath, returning to Cow on the next inhale and Cat on the next exhale.
Repeat for 5–10 cycles, maintaining smooth, even breathing throughout.

cat-cow-stretch.breathing: Synchronize each movement with a full inhalation or exhalation, keeping the breath steady and unforced.

common_mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders relaxed and away from ears

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting hips sag or lift too high
common_mistakes.fix: Maintain hips level over knees throughout

easier: Place a folded blanket under the knees for extra cushioning
Perform the movement while seated on a chair, using the same inhale‑exhale pattern
harder: Add a gentle arm reach forward on the inhale to deepen the extension
Transition into a low lunge after each Cow for added hip stretch
avoid_if: Recent spinal surgery or severe back injury

plank-pose.name: Plank Pose
plank-pose.summary: Plank Pose is a full‑body hold that strengthens the core, shoulders, and legs. It is used to build stability, endurance, and calorie burn for weight‑loss goals.
benefits: Improves core strength and spinal stability
Increases muscular endurance across the whole body

steps.text: Start in Adho Mukha Svanasana (Downward Dog) with hands shoulder‑width apart and feet hip‑width apart
Shift weight forward, lowering the hips until shoulders are directly over wrists
Straighten the legs, pressing the heels toward the floor, forming a straight line from head to heels
Engage the core, draw the belly button toward the spine, and squeeze the glutes
Hold the position, keeping the neck neutral and gaze slightly forward

plank-pose.breathing: Maintain steady, even breaths, inhaling and exhaling through the nose or mouth as comfortable.

common_mistakes.fix: Press the hips up and engage the core to keep a straight line
Roll the shoulders down and away from the ears

easier: Drop to the knees while keeping the same alignment
Place hands on an elevated surface such as a block or low bench
harder: Lift one leg a few inches off the floor
Transition to forearm plank (Phalakasana variation)
props: Yoga block under hands to reduce wrist extension
avoid_if: Wrist pain or carpal tunnel syndrome

tree-pose.name: Tree Pose
tree-pose.summary: Tree Pose is a standing balance that strengthens the legs and core while sharpening concentration. It is often used to develop steadiness and mental focus.

steps.text: Begin in Tadasana (Mountain Pose) with feet hip‑width apart
Shift weight onto your left foot, grounding the foot evenly
Bend the right knee and place the right foot on the inner left thigh or calf, avoiding the knee joint
Press the foot into the leg and the leg into the foot, engaging the standing thigh
Bring the hands to prayer position at the heart or raise them overhead, lengthening the spine
Find a steady gaze (drishti) and hold the pose

tree-pose.breathing: Maintain slow, even breaths, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the balance.

common_mistakes.mistake: Foot placed too high on the knee
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the foot below the knee joint on the thigh or calf
Engage the core and draw the standing hip inward toward the midline

easier: Place the foot lower on the shin instead of the thigh
Use a wall for light support
Keep hands at the heart instead of overhead
harder: Close the eyes to challenge proprioception
Extend arms overhead with palms facing each other
Transition from Tree Pose into a standing forward bend without returning to Tadasana
props: Yoga block under the lifted foot for added stability

paschimottanasana-seated-forward-fold.name: Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Fold)
paschimottanasana-seated-forward-fold.summary: Paschimottanasana is a seated forward bend that lengthens the spine and stretches the hamstrings. It is practiced to improve flexibility and calm the nervous system.

steps.text: Sit with legs extended straight in front of you
Sit up tall, reaching the crown of your head toward the ceiling
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping the spine long
Reach for your feet, shins, or a strap, allowing the torso to fold
Relax the neck and shoulders, maintaining a straight back as you deepen the fold
Hold the position, breathing deeply and evenly

paschimottanasana-seated-forward-fold.breathing: Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to deepen the fold, then breathe smoothly throughout the hold.

common_mistakes.fix: Lead with the hips and keep the spine long
Use a strap or rest hands on shins, focus on the stretch, not the reach

easier: Place a folded blanket under the hips
Use a yoga strap around the feet
Bend the knees slightly
harder: Grab the big toes and pull gently for a deeper stretch
Straighten the legs fully and engage the quadriceps
Add a gentle twist by reaching opposite hand to opposite foot
props: Yoga strap: helps reach the feet without rounding
Blanket under hips: supports lower back
Block: place under hands for extra reach
avoid_if: Severe lower back injury or herniated disc

virabhadrasana-ii-warrior-ii.name: Virabhadrasana II (Warrior II)
virabhadrasana-ii-warrior-ii.summary: Warrior II is a standing strength pose that builds leg endurance and opens the hips. It also improves focus and stability for everyday activities.

steps.text: Stand with feet wide apart, about 3–4 feet distance
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and align the heel with the arch of the left foot
Turn your left foot in slightly, keeping the heel grounded
Bend your right knee over the ankle, thigh parallel to the floor
Extend both arms parallel to the floor, palms down, reaching actively
Gaze over the right fingertips, keeping the neck long
Hold for 30–60 seconds, then release and repeat on the other side

virabhadrasana-ii-warrior-ii.breathing: Maintain steady, diaphragmatic breathing, inhaling as you open the chest and exhaling as you deepen the bend.

common_mistakes.fix: Press the knee toward the second toe to keep alignment

common_mistakes.mistake: Hips tilt toward the back leg
common_mistakes.fix: Square the hips forward, engaging the core

easier: Place a block under the front hand for support
Shorten the stance width
Bend the back knee slightly
harder: Lift the back heel off the ground
Sink deeper into the front knee bend
Add a bind by threading the rear arm under the front arm
props: Yoga block under front hand to maintain arm height
avoid_if: Recent knee injury or ligament strain
High blood pressure with uncontrolled spikes

matsyasana-fish-pose.name: Matsyasana (Fish Pose)
matsyasana-fish-pose.summary: Fish Pose is a supine backbend that opens the chest and throat, helping counteract forward‑rounded posture. It is practiced to increase thoracic mobility and promote a feeling of openness in the upper body.
benefits: Opens the chest for better breathing

steps.text: Lie on your back with legs extended and arms resting beside you, palms down
Slide your hands under your hips, elbows close to your body, palms pressing into the floor
Press firmly through your forearms and lift your chest, creating an arch in the upper back
Allow the crown of your head to gently rest on the floor, keeping the neck relaxed
Hold the position, keeping most of the weight on your forearms and shoulders
To release, slowly lower your chest and head back to the mat

matsyasana-fish-pose.breathing: Maintain smooth, even breathing, inhaling as you lift the chest and exhaling as you settle deeper into the arch.

common_mistakes.fix: Rest only the crown lightly; support with a folded blanket if needed
Keep elbows close together to protect shoulders

easier: Place a folded blanket under the head for neck support
Bend knees slightly to reduce lumbar strain
harder: Straighten legs and engage the core for a deeper arch
Lift one leg off the floor while maintaining the chest lift
props: Blanket under head – cushions the neck
Yoga block between forearms – adds stability
avoid_if: Severe neck injury or cervical spine instability

marichyasana-marichi-s-pose.name: Marichyasana (Marichi's Pose)
marichyasana-marichi-s-pose.summary: Marichyasana is a seated spinal twist that stretches the back, shoulders, and hips. It is practiced to improve spinal mobility, aid digestion, and release tension.

steps.text: Sit tall with legs extended forward, grounding both sitting bones.
Bend the right knee, placing the right foot flat beside the left thigh.
Wrap the left arm around the right shin, hugging the knee toward the chest.
Place the right hand behind you, fingers pointing forward or resting on the floor.
Lengthen the spine, then gently twist to the right, looking over the right shoulder.
Maintain even breathing, keeping the hips square and the lower back long.

marichyasana-marichi-s-pose.breathing: Breathe smoothly and evenly, using the breath to deepen the twist on each exhale.

common_mistakes.fix: Lengthen the tailbone toward the floor before twisting
Draw shoulder blades down and away from ears

easier: Sit on a folded blanket for extra hip support
Place a strap around the bent knee to assist the arm wrap
harder: Bind the opposite arm around the back leg for a deeper bind
Straighten the bent leg and twist over the extended leg
props: Blanket under sit bones for cushioning
Yoga strap to help bind the arm around the shin

legs-up-the-wall.name: Legs Up the Wall
legs-up-the-wall.summary: Legs Up the Wall is a gentle, inverted restorative pose that eases circulation and calms the nervous system. It is used to relieve tired legs, reduce swelling, and promote relaxation.
benefits: Helps you wind down before sleep
Improves venous return to the heart

steps.text: Lie on your back on a comfortable mat with your hips a few inches from the wall
Scoot your sitting bones so that your lower back is close to the wall
Swing your legs up, resting the backs of your calves against the wall; adjust distance for comfort
Allow your arms to rest by your sides, palms facing up
Close your eyes, soften your shoulders, and breathe slowly and evenly
Stay for the desired time, then gently bend knees and slide down the wall

legs-up-the-wall.breathing: Maintain slow, diaphragmatic breaths, inhaling through the nose and exhaling through the nose or mouth.

common_mistakes.mistake: Legs too far from the wall, causing strain in the lower back
common_mistakes.fix: Move closer until the backs of the calves comfortably touch the wall

common_mistakes.mistake: Neck turned to one side, creating tension
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the neck neutral, eyes closed or gazing upward

easier: Place a folded blanket or bolster under the sacrum for gentle support
Bend knees slightly to reduce inversion intensity
harder: Let the legs open into a wide straddle against the wall
Add a gentle hip opener by placing a strap around the thighs
props: Blanket under sacrum – supports lower back
Bolster against the wall – reduces pressure on calves
avoid_if: Severe glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure
Recent eye surgery or retinal issues
Deep vein thrombosis (ask your doctor first)

twisted-triangle.name: Twisted Triangle
twisted-triangle.summary: Twisted Triangle is a standing balance that combines a lateral stretch with a spinal twist. It helps improve digestion, detoxify the torso, and builds leg strength.

steps.text: Stand with feet wide apart, about 3–4 feet, grounding evenly through both feet
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and align the heel with the arch of your left foot
Square your hips toward the front of the mat while keeping the left heel slightly turned in
Place your left hand on the right shin, ankle, or the floor beside the right foot
Reach your right arm up, opening the chest, and gently twist the torso to the right, looking toward the right hand
Keep both legs straight but avoid locking the knees; engage the thigh muscles
Hold the twist, breathing evenly, then release and repeat on the opposite side

twisted-triangle.breathing: Maintain smooth, steady breaths, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the twist.

common_mistakes.fix: Open the ribs and keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Maintain a micro‑bend in the knees to protect the joints
Turn the gaze toward the lifted hand to encourage a deeper twist

easier: Place a yoga block under the hand that reaches the floor
Use a chair for support, sitting on the edge and performing the twist seated
harder: Deepen the twist by reaching the lifted arm overhead and gazing at the thumb
Bring the bottom hand to the floor outside the front foot
props: Yoga block: supports the hand if the floor is unreachable
avoid_if: High blood pressure that worsens with twisting

happy-baby.name: Happy Baby
happy-baby.summary: Happy Baby is a supine hip opener that gently stretches the inner thighs and lower back while promoting relaxation. It is often used to release tension after a vigorous practice or to calm the nervous system.

steps.text: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor
Draw both knees toward your chest, hugging them with your arms
Reach for the outer edges of the feet with your hands, keeping the arms on the inside of the knees
Open the knees wider than your torso, allowing the ankles to flex outward
Gently rock side to side, finding a comfortable range of motion
Hold the position, breathing calmly for 30–60 seconds

happy-baby.breathing: Maintain slow, diaphragmatic breaths, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the hip opening.

common_mistakes.mistake: Gripping the toes instead of the outer edges of the feet
common_mistakes.fix: Hold the outer edges of the soles to keep shoulders relaxed

common_mistakes.mistake: Pressing the lower back into the floor forcefully
common_mistakes.fix: Allow a gentle arch; keep the lower back relaxed

easier: Place a yoga strap around the soles of the feet and hold the strap
Use a folded blanket under the head for support
harder: Straighten the knees while keeping the hips flexed
Hold longer, rocking gently side to side
props: Yoga strap – helps reach the feet without straining the shou
Blanket under the head – provides neck comfort

sun-salutation-a.name: Sun Salutation A
sun-salutation-a.summary: Sun Salutation A is a linked series of standing, forward‑fold, plank and back‑bending postures performed in a smooth flow. It raises heart rate, warms the muscles and prepares the body for deeper work.

steps.text: Start in Tadasana, feet together, arms at heart center
Sweep arms overhead, gaze upward
Fold forward, hands to the floor or shins
Lift torso halfway, lengthen spine, hands on shins
Step back one foot at a time into Plank Pose
Lower slowly to the floor, keeping elbows close (low push‑up)
Slide forward, roll onto the tops of the feet, lift chest into Bhujangasana
Press back into Adho Mukha Svanasana, hips high
Step right foot forward between hands, rise to standing

sun-salutation-a.breathing: Match each movement with a steady, diaphragmatic breath, inhaling on opening actions and exhaling on folding or lowering actions.

common_mistakes.fix: Engage shoulder blades and keep a straight line from head to heels
Press the tops of the feet into the mat and lift chest without collapsing the lumbar spine

easier: Place hands on blocks for the forward fold
Drop knees to the mat in the low push‑up
harder: Add a jump back to plank instead of stepping
Lift one leg in Downward Dog for balance
props: Yoga blocks under hands in forward fold to maintain length

corpse-pose.name: Corpse Pose
corpse-pose.summary: Savasana is a supine resting posture used at the end of a yoga session to integrate the practice. It promotes deep relaxation and helps the nervous system shift toward parasympathetic dominance.
benefits: Helps the body shift into a resting state
Reduces feelings of stress and anxiety

steps.text: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and feet falling naturally open
Allow your arms to rest alongside the body, palms facing upward
Close your eyes and soften the facial muscles
Take slow, natural breaths, feeling the rise and fall of the abdomen
Mentally scan the body, releasing tension from each muscle group
Stay in the position for the desired duration, maintaining relaxed breathing

corpse-pose.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose, allowing the breath to become effortless.

common_mistakes.fix: Use a small pillow or folded blanket to keep the head centered

common_mistakes.mistake: Raising the shoulders toward the ears
common_mistakes.fix: Drop the shoulders away from the ears and relax the neck

easier: Place a bolster under the knees to relieve lower back
Use a folded blanket under the head for neck support
harder: Extend the stay to 15 minutes or incorporate a guided body scan
props: Blanket under the head for neck comfort
Bolster or folded blanket under the knees to support the low
avoid_if: Lower back discomfort lying flat (bend the knees or put a bolster under them)
Pregnancy beyond the first trimester (rest on your side instead)
Feeling anxious with eyes closed (keep them softly open)

utthita-trikonasana-triangle-pose.name: Utthita Trikonasana (Triangle Pose)
utthita-trikonasana-triangle-pose.summary: Triangle Pose is a standing stretch that opens the sides of the torso and lengthens the hamstrings while building leg strength. It is practiced to improve balance, spinal alignment, and overall flexibility.

steps.text: Stand with feet wide apart, grounding evenly through both feet
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and align the heel with the left heel
Square your right heel with the left heel, then hinge at the hip to the right, reaching the right hand toward the floor
Place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or a block, and extend the left arm toward the ceiling
Lengthen both sides of the waist, gaze up toward the left hand, and breathe evenly

utthita-trikonasana-triangle-pose.breathing: Maintain steady, even breaths, inhaling as you open the torso and exhaling as you deepen the hinge.

common_mistakes.fix: Engage the ribcage and keep the chest open toward the ceiling
Roll shoulders down and away from ears

easier: Place a yoga block under the bottom hand
Practise with your back against a wall for alignment
harder: Lower the bottom hand to the floor outside the front foot
Reach the top hand overhead for a full lengthening
props: Block: supports the lower hand when reaching the floor
Chair: sit on it for a seated version of the pose
avoid_if: Recent hip replacement or severe hip pain

setu-bandhasana-bridge-pose.name: Setu Bandhasana (Bridge Pose)
setu-bandhasana-bridge-pose.summary: Bridge Pose is a supine backbend that lifts the spine and opens the chest. It is used to strengthen the back, glutes, and hamstrings while relieving mild back discomfort.
benefits: Opens the chest and improves posture

steps.text: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor
Place feet hip‑width apart, heels a few inches from your sit bones
Press through the feet, engage the thighs, and lift the hips toward the ceiling
Interlace fingers under your back, rolling the shoulders back and down
Keep knees tracking over the ankles and thighs parallel
Hold the lift, drawing the shoulder blades together, for the desired time

setu-bandhasana-bridge-pose.breathing: Maintain steady, diaphragmatic breathing, inhaling to lengthen the spine and exhaling to deepen the lift.

common_mistakes.fix: Engage the glutes and press firmly through the heels
Keep the neck neutral, gaze toward the ceiling or gently close eyes

easier: Place a yoga block or folded blanket under the sacrum for support
Bend the knees more to reduce the lift height
harder: Interlace the fingers under your back and roll onto the shoulders
Lift one leg while maintaining the bridge for added core challenge
props: Yoga block under sacrum – provides gentle support and reduce
avoid_if: Recent spinal disc injury or severe osteoporosis
Acute lower‑back pain or herniated disc

sirsasana-headstand.name: Sirsasana (Headstand)
sirsasana-headstand.summary: Headstand is an inverted balance pose performed on the crown of the head and forearms. It is practiced to improve circulation, strengthen the core and shoulder girdle, and enhance mental focus.

steps.text: Kneel and place forearms on the floor, elbows shoulder‑width apart
Interlace fingers and create a cup for the crown of the head
Place the crown of the head in the cupped hands, keeping neck neutral
Tuck toes, lift hips up, and walk feet toward elbows to build a tripod base
Slowly lift one leg, then the other, coming to a full vertical line
Engage the core, keep legs straight, and find a steady gaze
Hold the pose for the desired time, maintaining even breathing
To exit, gently lower one leg at a time back to the floor
Rest in Child's Pose to release the neck and spine

sirsasana-headstand.breathing: Maintain slow, steady diaphragmatic breaths throughout, inhaling to prepare and exhaling to stabilize the pose.

common_mistakes.fix: Keep the crown of the head lightly resting in the hands, never bearing full load

common_mistakes.mistake: Hips sag or rise too high
common_mistakes.fix: Engage the core and glutes to keep the spine in a straight line
Press through the forearms and keep the core tight to stabilize the legs

easier: Place a folded blanket under the forearms for extra cushioning
Practise at a wall, lifting one leg at a time with control (never kick up)
harder: Practice a split‑leg variation (straddle)
Enter the pose with Lotus legs for increased hip flexibility
props: Yoga block under forearms to reduce wrist strain
Wall behind for safety during learning
avoid_if: You have not learned it with a qualified teacher yet

savasana-corpse-pose.name: Savasana (Corpse Pose)
savasana-corpse-pose.summary: Savasana is a supine resting posture performed at the end of a yoga session. It allows the nervous system to reset and integrates the physical and mental benefits of the practice.
benefits: Helps the body shift into a resting state

steps.text: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and feet falling naturally apart
Allow your feet to relax outward and let your knees soften if needed
Place your arms alongside your body, palms facing upward
Close your eyes and soften your facial muscles
Scan your body and consciously release tension from each muscle group
Shift attention to the natural rhythm of your breath without trying to change it
Remain still and present for the allotted time, gently returning focus if the mind wanders

savasana-corpse-pose.breathing: Maintain a smooth, natural breath, observing the inhale and exhale without forcing them.

common_mistakes.mistake: Legs are too close together causing tension in hips
common_mistakes.fix: Allow knees to fall open naturally

common_mistakes.mistake: Head is turned to one side causing neck strain
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the head centered and use a small pillow if needed

easier: Place a folded blanket under the knees to relieve lower back
Use a bolster under the torso for extra support
harder: Extend the pose to 20 minutes for deeper relaxation
Practice with eyes slightly open focusing on a distant point
props: Blanket under knees – reduces lumbar pressure
Bolster under torso – supports a gentle chest lift
Eye pillow – blocks light and enhances relaxation
avoid_if: Lower back discomfort lying flat (bend the knees or put a bolster under them)
Pregnancy beyond the first trimester (rest on your side instead)
Feeling anxious with eyes closed (keep them softly open)
